sentences.text:
15.11.2023 Order No. (Through hybrid mode)
01.

1. Heard Ms. M. Sahoo, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. S.S. Pradhan, learned Addl.
Government Advocate for the State.
2.

This is an application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the petitioner in connection with Mahulpali P.S. Case No. 73 of 2023 corresponding to Special G.R. Case No.26 of 2023 pending in the Court of the learned Addl. Sessions Judge -cum- Special Court (under POCSO Act),
Sambalpur under Sections 376(2)(n), 323, 506, 34 of IPC read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act.

3. The petitioner had moved an application for bail before the Court of learned Addl. Sessions Judge -cum- Special Court (under POCSO Act), Sambalpur which was rejected on 17.10.2023.
4.
The prosecution allegation in brief is that on 09.02.2023 one Sukanta Kisan was in love with the daughter of the informant and took her to his house assuring to marry her.
They have spent their life as husband and wife in his house and had physical relations on a number of occasions.
Thereafter he assaulted her and drove her out.
When the victim tried to contact the present petitioner, his mother and father did not allow her.
On 30.06.2023 all of them assaulted the victim and threatened to kill her.
So she returned to her house and narrated everything to her family members.
She had sustained injury on her left ankle due to their assault.
5. Ms. M. Sahoo, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in custody since 02.07.2023.

She further submits that victim had gone voluntarily with the petitioner in her house and stayed there for about 7 to 8 months and thereafter, she left his house on account of some disturbance, for which the offence under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC is not be made out against him.

sentences.text: She also submits that the victim and her mother-informant have been examined during trial and hence there is no question of the petitioner tampering with the evidence if he is released on bail at this stage.
Copy of the depositions of P.Ws.1 to 6 filed by the learned counsel for the petitioner are taken on record.

6. Mr. S.S. Pradhan, learned Addl. Government Advocate for the State opposes the prayer for bail stating that the victim was a minor on the date of occurrence and the petitioner has taken her to his house and kept her there for a few months and thereafter thrown her out without any justifiable cause.

Since the consent of a minor is no consent in the eye of law, offence under Section 376(2)(n)
of IPC is squarely made out against the petitioner.
He further submits that the trial has commenced in the case and if the petitioner released on bail, he will tamper with the evidence and threaten the prosecution witnesses.

7. Considering the nature of allegations against the petitioner, the period of his detention in custody,
the age of the petitioner and the deposition of the victim and her mother-informant, I am inclined to allow the prayer for bail.
8. Let the petitioner- Sukanta Kisan be released on bail on such terms and conditions as may be fixed by the learned Court below in seisin over the matter including the following conditions:
( i) He shall not go near the house of the victim girl or try to contact her unless it is for the purpose of marriage.
(ii) He will not try to influence or threaten the prosecution witnesses.
(iii) He will report before the Mahulpali Police Station every alternate Sunday between 11.00 A.M. to 2.00 P.M. till conclusion of trial.

(iv) He shall remain present in Court on each date it is fixed for trial and not seek unnecessary adjournments.
9.
Violation of any condition will entail in cancellation of bail.
10. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
11. Any observations in this order should not influence the learned trial Court, as they have been made for the purpose of considering the prayer for bail.
12. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.

13. A copy of this order be supplied to Mr. S.S. Pradhan, learned Addl. Government Advocate for the State for onward transmission to the I.I.C., Mahulpali Police Station.
